r.name: Peace How Walk From High Brandelhow Jetty, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: A gentle walk with time & space to reflect. Peace How looks over Derwent Water to the north, & Castle Crag – a WW1 memorial fell – to the south. It was gifted to NT in 1917, so that anyone affected by the WW1 could come & experience peace & tranquility.

r.name: Thorneythwaite Farm Picnic and Waterfall walk, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: This short walk introduces you to the 3 parts of a hill farm – the in-bye land, in-take land & open fell. You'll see hay meadows & gradually restored wood pasture. Climb to discover a hidden valley & a beautiful waterfall – all overlooked by Coombe Crag.

r.name: Octavia Hill walk at Brandelhow Park, Derwent Water, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: An easy lakeside amble along the quiet side of Derwent Water, leading you on a circular route through the tranquil parkland at Brandelhow, birthplace of the National Trust in the Lake District. Low-level lakeside and woodland paths.

r.name: Walla Crag to Ashness Bridge walk, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: Through valleys, over streams & up to spectacular viewpoints, the landscape here near Derwent Water, the ‘Jewel of the Lake District’ is magnificent in every season. Enjoy the timeless beauty of Ashness Bridge, the lake & Skiddaw as a backdrop.

r.name: Borger Dalr Geology Walk, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: Explore the origins of Borrowdale as you walk from Bowder Stone car park to Castle Crag, including the poignant war memorial Peace Howe, and amazing views of the flat valley bed that was formerly the bottom of an Ice Age lake. A steep but gradual climb.

r.name: Castle Crag from Seatoller Trail: The Scenic Route, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: Scaling Castle Crag from Seatoller starts with a bit of a climb, then follows a rolling contour route giving you great views right across the valley. This is definitely the civilized way to climb Castle Crag. Steep climbs and uneven paths in places.

r.name: Rosthwaite Round, Fells, Tarn and Beck Walk, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: This favourite walk of National Trust rangers will take you to a Borrowdale gem, the hamlet of Watendlath. Along the way, you'll discover oak woodland, two tarns (mountain ponds) and stunning Lakeland views.

r.name: Seatoller, Styhead Tarn and Grains Gill Walk, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: An invigorating circular into the the Lakeland fells beyond Borrowdale. Follow an ancient packhorse route, as mountain views of Great End & Great Gable rise above you. Relax by Sprinkling Tarn before returning via Grains Gill stream. Rugged rock paths.

r.name: Force Crag Mine Accessible Trail, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: Linear there and back walk along Coledale Beck to Force Crag Mine.

r.name: Accessible walk to Broomhill Point, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: A stile-free out & back along Derwent Water to Broomhill Point. Views of Cat Bells & Causey Pike. Choice at Strandshag bay; a smooth compact surface or nearer the lake with boulders, tree roots & mud. One 16% gradient on bumpy surface & 2m wide boardwalk

r.name: Castle Head Viewpoint, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: A short linear walk to Castle Head. Views of Derwent Water.

r.name: Great Wood Walk, North Lakes Outdoors
r.description: A walk round Great Wood, a protected and internationally significant ancient Atlantic oak woodland. Spot lichens, fungi and red squirrels from waymarked walks.

r.name: Lakeside Amble, North Lakes Outdoors
Downstream to Derwent Walk, Borrowdale and Derwent Water
r.description: Can catch the Honister Rambler bus back to the car park, note that this service only runs seasonally. Steady downhill walk, there is a steep, rocky section with a chain to hold for support. It can get very slippery in wet weather.
